findings.text: The first lede tells a newcomer what Athena is and what sets it apart. It does this in two plain sentences before any detail.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The page says why it exists: it is a worked example of what Athena can do. The case for why a newcomer should care about Athena rests on this example alone, and nothing else on the page supports it.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: There is a link to next steps in the header, so a newcomer finds out early what to do. The Next steps section names the repository, an install command and a first request to try.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The install step assumes the reader already has a checkout of the repository and the tools it needs. It gives no clone command and no prerequisites, such as a Rust toolchain or AI model access, so the reader has to go to the repository to learn them.
findings.source: Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh

findings.text: The Start here section serves newcomers well. It defines its words before using them, gives a one-sentence description of firstmate, and walks one task from Queued to Done in numbered steps.

Some terms are never defined in the Glossary, including endpoint, wake, harness pin and captain-held inventory. Others appear only in claims, such as "main first mate". In the transition cards, these words make the text hard going for a stranger.
findings.source: a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine and 44 claims about firstmate. That is thorough and checkable, but someone who came for Athena gets far more firstmate detail than they need to understand Athena.
findings.source: States of a piece of work / Transitions / Claims and sources

findings.text: The page says plainly where its sources go quiet: on in scope, on retry limits and on captain deadlines. The Limits of this study section also says nothing was run. This builds trust, but it leaves some firstmate behaviour unexplained.
findings.source: The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it.

findings.text: The early definitions repeat word for word in the Glossary. This makes the page longer for a first-time reader without telling them anything new.
findings.source: Words used first ... Each is defined here, and again in the Glossary at the end of the page.
